text:
michael.s: incident-bot paging: ELB health checks failing across us-east-1a and us-east-1b, elevated 5xx for /api/v1/generate. Alert threshold hit at 13:12 UTC.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Severity P1 - Serving degradation detected in us-east-1. Pages sent to on-call rota. Incident channel: #inc-1819005555
Sara.k: I'm on it, looking at CloudWatch right now. Seeing a surge in 504/502 from the NLB -> targetgroup.
ben.t: Confirming, target group TG-app-prod-us-east has ~40% unhealthy in us-east-1b, and cross-zone latency spikes.
Priya.r: Route53 health checks also showing slow resolution to ELB CNAMEs from multiple regions; might be partial DNS propagation or a regional Route53 issue.
lia: I'm checking ASG and EC2 console. No large scale instance terminations. EC2 metrics for the app fleet are normal CPU.
ops-bot: deploy-bot reports no deploys in last 30m. No config changes detected.
michael.s: Good. Let's collect impact: customer-facing error rate up ~18% for reads, 25% for writes. Some VIPs reporting timeouts. Can we fail traffic to us-west-2 as temporary mitigation?
ben.t: Canary failover for specific customers is possible via per-customer routing in the API gateway, but global customers get DNS-backed endpoints. For mass traffic, need Route53 failover policy or update ELB cross-zone config.
Priya.r: AWS Health Dashboard shows a "Networking/ELB" anomaly in us-east-1 starting 12:58 UTC: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ - looks regional.
Sara.k: Trying to confirm whether it's ELB control plane or data plane. I'm seeing TCP resets at the ELB -> targets. Elb logs show 502s with message: 
```
[elb] 2026-03-15T13:05:20Z ... "502" "no healthy upstream"
```

lia: Stacktrace from one host: upstream read timeout, but the host was healthy per local checks. Suggests connectivity between ELB and target ENIs is flaky.
incident-bot: @oncall escalation: paging schedule forwarded to ben.t (primary) and michael.s (backup)
ben.t: I'll coordinate with AWS support now. Opening a support case (case #1234567890). Copying relevant logs.
ben.t: Also spinning up an isolated ALB in us-east-1c and re-registering a subset of instances to see if we can get healthy traffic slices.
michael.s: Meanwhile ops: add temporary R53 weighted failover for /api to route 80% -> us-west-2, 20% -> us-east-1 to reduce load and customer impact. Make sure TTL is low.
Priya.r: Creating a Route53 change: set weight 80/20 and set TTL = 60s. Applying now.
ops-bot: Route53 change submitted: change id Z3ABCXYZC1.
Sara.k: Observing a drop in error rate within 3 minutes. Some customers still stuck due to DNS cache, but overall 5xx reduced from 25% -> 8% across global synth checks. :thumbsup: 
ben.t: AWS support says they're investigating ELB control plane and internal networking between AZs. No ETA yet. They suggested traffic shift as mitigation.
lia: For customers pinned to us-east-1 via regional endpoints, we should open a support ticket per account. Not feasible at scale. Can we set a temporary reverse-proxy in us-west to front requests?
michael.s: Not in the next 10m. Keep DNS shift and monitor. Notify SRE pager and Customer Success to draft customer comms.
Priya.r: On-call handoff in 20m to Sara. @Sara.k you'll take second-shift.
Sara.k: Copy, I'll take the 15:30-19:30 UTC shift. Logging notes in #inc-1819005555.
ben.t: Pushed an autoscaling tweak: increase min-size in us-west for the short term and warm up extra targets. Also disabled cross-zone load balancing on the problematic ELB to reduce cross-AZ flapping.
lia: Disabling cross-zone seemed to reduce backend rejections on a trial ALB; monitoring for 5 minutes.
ops-bot: metric-monitor reports 5xx_count down to 6% globally, latency stable.
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 13:34 UTC due to mitigation and reduced customer impact.
Priya.r: CS drafting message: "We are investigating a regional AWS networking issue impacting some requests. We've shifted traffic to an alternate region and are monitoring. We'll provide an update in 30 minutes." Approving.
michael.s: Great. Start a runbook doc in /confluence/incidents/1819005555 (I'll own). Add timeline and actions.
ben.t: AWS now says they identified issues with AZ-local ENI connectivity that caused ELB health propagation delays. They will apply mitigation and monitor. No ETA but they're seeing improvement.
Sara.k: FYI some customers on corporate networks still see high latency—likely DNS TTLs and ISP caching. Recommend adding a note in CS message about clearing local caches and expected propagation time.
lia: Now seeing SYN retransmits between ELB and some targets in 1b; 1c looks healthy. Seems AZ-scoped networking quirk.
michael.s: Handoff to Sara in 18 minutes. Ben, please keep AWS case open and capture timeline. Priya, coordinate CS. Lia, keep metrics and traces. Ops-bot, continue automated runbook checks.
ben.t: AWS updated case: "Control plane reconciliation underway. Expected full resolution within 60-120 minutes, but no firm ETA." Logged update to case.
incident-bot: Reminder: please update on-call status before handoff.
Priya.r: CS message sent to affected customers at 13:47 UTC.
Sara.k: Taking over incident at 14:10 UTC (handoff recorded). Notes: traffic weighted to us-west, Route53 TTL 60s, ALB cross-zone disabled on problematic ELB, additional instances in us-west warming.
lia: Post-mitigation checks: synthetic checks across apac/eu show <2% 5xx; us-east residual 5xx ~4% due to caching. Traces show increased p95 latency for a short window but normalizing.
ben.t: AWS health update: "Service impact reduced. Customers should see continued improvement. Follow-up postmortem to be provided."
michael.s: We'll keep the incident open til full recovery and AWS final confirmation. Plan: rotate back traffic gradually after AWS OK and keep TTL low for 30 minutes post-change.
Priya.r: Filing incident ticket for postmortem with owners: michael.s (lead), ben.t (AWS liaison), sara.k (metrics), lia (network checks), priya.r (customer comms).
ops-bot: Scheduled follow-up: postmortem doc creation reminder in 24h.
incident-bot: Incident closed for active paging at 15:24 UTC. Please ensure postmortem sections completed.
ben.t: Saving all logs, ELB access logs, Route53 changes, CloudTrail events into the incident S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1819005555/
Sara.k: Quick remediation notes to include in PM: - Short-term DNS weighted failover; - Disable cross-zone ELB on affected ELB; - Increase warm pool in alternate region; - Customer comms template.
lia: I'll attach tcpdumps and tcp retransmit graphs.
michael.s: Thanks team. We’ll triage root cause with AWS after we get the postmortem. Closing active slack thread in 1h.
incident-bot: Final status: customers affected: partial (some timeouts and elevated latency). Duration: ~1.5 hours of elevated errors. Actions taken: traffic shift, ALB config change, instance warmup, CS notifications.
Sara.k: Adding timeline entries and final metrics to the postmortem doc now.
Priya.r: Ping me when the doc is ready so I can finalize the customer-facing summary.
ben.t: Case #1234567890 awaiting AWS post-incident report.
michael.s: End of thread.
